title: Scoring Against References: Exact, Lexical and Semantic
summary: When you have a reference answer, you can score outputs automatically. This lesson builds exact match, token F1, BLEU and ROUGE, embedding similarity and code-based checks by hand, and shows exactly where each one breaks.
objectives: Normalise answers and compute exact match and token-level F1 by hand
Explain n-gram precision (BLEU) and longest-common-subsequence recall (ROUGE-L) and compute small examples
Score answers with embedding cosine similarity and explain why negation and numbers defeat it
Use programmatic checks and estimate pass@k from repeated samples
Pick a reference metric for a task and name its failure cases
prerequisites: Precision, recall and F1 from [Success Criteria](/learn/evaluation/success-criteria). Cosine similarity is introduced from scratch, but [Embeddings](/learn/model-foundations/embeddings) gives useful background.
